title: 5 Rules for Better Tooltips
summary: This reel outlines five essential rules for designing user-friendly tooltips, focusing on timing, visual clarity, and responsiveness. It teaches how to avoid common pitfalls like 'noisy' instant triggers and content that gets cut off by screen edges.

transcript.text: Rule 1: Wait 300 milliseconds before showing. Instant tooltips fire every time a cursor passes by. That is noise, not help. Intent, not accidents.
Rule 2: Point with an arrow. The tail connects the tooltip to its trigger. Without it, users cannot tell what you are explaining. Arrows remove all doubt.
Rule 3: Flip near viewport edges. A tooltip cut off by the screen is worse than no tooltip at all. Detect the edge, flip the position. Detect viewport bounds. Adjust anchor.
Rule 4: Dismiss everywhere. Mouse leave, Escape key, Focus out, tap outside. A sticky tooltip traps the user. Every escape route matters.
Rule 5: Keep it tight. Maximum 300 pixels wide. One sentence maximum. A tooltip is a hint, not documentation.
Save this before your next tooltip. Follow for more micro UX rules.

before_after: A transformation from a 'cheap' tooltip (instant, no arrow, long text, cut off by edges) to a 'premium' tooltip (delayed, arrowed, concise, and responsive).
